q: How do I find a specific item in the RizzitGO spreadsheet?
a: Start with the model name or one distinctive feature. If the seller uses a different name, remove the brand term, choose a category and compare the listing photos. Save the item ID when you find a match.

q: How do I browse beyond the first page of finds?
a: Use the page number beside the catalogue results. The range above the cards shows which items you are viewing out of the filtered total. Clear your category and search terms to return to the complete catalogue.

q: Why does the catalogue have more pages on my phone?
a: Mobile pages show 20 products at a time. Desktop pages can show 60. Compare the total item count above the cards when switching devices. The same item ID opens the same listing on either device.

q: Why does the same product appear under different names?
a: Sellers can describe similar items differently, and a translated title can omit a model code. Compare the item ID, seller link and variant photos before treating two listings as identical.

q: How can I search for an item using my own photo?
a: Open the camera beside the search box and select a photo. Crop it around one item, leaving its outline visible. Open a result and compare its details with the original before choosing a variant.

q: Which photo works best for visual search?
a: A clear photograph of one item against a plain background gives you a good starting point. For a collage or outfit, first crop to the shoe, bag or garment you want. Try a second angle if the results mostly match the background.

q: Does a similar image prove it is the same product?
a: Images can be reused across listings. Compare construction details, the item ID and seller options. For a shoe, inspect the panel shapes, sole and logo placement as well as the overall colour.

q: What is the difference between listing, style and QC photos?
a: Listing images introduce the item. Style images help you select a seller option. QC images show a photographed unit under warehouse conditions. Check the selected variant before using any photo to judge a prospective purchase.

q: How do I copy a Weidian link for a specific style?
a: Open the listing, select its colour, size and any other required option, then use the copy button. Reopen the link and confirm the selected variant. If the seller only supplies an item-level link, record the option names separately.

q: What should I do if my copied link opens the default colour?
a: Compare the product ID, then reselect the saved colour and size on the destination page. Send the exact option labels with any order enquiry. A shared item URL can identify the listing without preserving all selections.

q: How do I open the same item on another buying platform?
a: Use the buying-agent menu on the detail page and choose an available destination. Check the marketplace item ID, selected variant, price and availability after the new page opens.

q: Why is a seller option missing or disabled?
a: An option can depend on another selection, or the seller may no longer offer that combination. Choose the colour first and review available sizes. Confirm live availability on the order page before paying.

q: How do I compare a seller’s size chart with my clothes?
a: Measure a similar garment laid flat and compare like with like. A flat chest width is half the corresponding circumference. Check units, measurement points and the difference between garment and body measurements.

q: What does changing currency on this site do?
a: The selector changes how catalogue prices are displayed. The buying platform shows the final payable amount at checkout. Review its currency, exchange rate and payment fees there.

q: Does the catalogue price include international shipping?
a: Treat the item price as one part of your budget. Check domestic delivery, any optional services, international freight and destination charges separately before deciding how much to spend.

q: What information should I enter in the freight calculator?
a: Use the destination, packed weight and parcel dimensions where requested. If packaging is still unknown, compare a compact estimate and a bulkier one. Recalculate after the warehouse measures the packed parcel.

q: Why can a large, light parcel cost more to ship?
a: Some routes calculate chargeable weight using package volume. A shoebox can use more transport space than folded clothing of similar weight. Compare route-specific estimates using the dimensions of the closed package.

q: Should I consolidate all my items into one parcel?
a: Compare the quotes, permitted item types and size limits for one parcel and for separate parcels. Consolidation may reduce repeated charges, but one bulky item can change the routes available for everything else.

q: What should I check before requesting international shipment?
a: Confirm the items, warehouse photos, delivery address, postcode and route restrictions. Save the final quote and service terms shown for that parcel before authorising dispatch.

q: Where can I track my RizzitGO parcel?
a: Use the tracking number from your shipment record on the official tracking page. A seller’s domestic tracking number follows the earlier trip to the warehouse and may refer to a different carrier.

q: Why is there no tracking update after the label was created?
a: A label can exist before the first physical carrier scan. Check the date, shipping stage and tracking number. If the displayed delivery window passes, contact support with the parcel ID and the last recorded event.

q: What QC photos should I look at before shipping a pair of shoes?
a: Check the pair together, both size labels, soles and the specific panels that identify your variant. If an important area is hidden, ask the buying platform whether an additional photo is available before dispatch.

q: What should I save if the warehouse receives the wrong item?
a: Keep the order number, selected variant, seller listing and a photo showing the mismatch. Contact the buying platform promptly from the order record so the case stays linked to the relevant item.

q: Can I return an item after international dispatch?
a: Check the order’s current stage and ask support for the applicable procedure, deadline and costs. Keep packaging and evidence until you receive instructions. A warehouse return and a return from your destination involve different shipping arrangements.
